text:
Alex: customer reported duplicate partial outputs + double billing after an SSE disconnect. they reconnect after ~45s and get a fresh generation plus resumed chunk, ends up charged twice.
Maria: ouch. do we have repro steps or a request id from them?
Alex: yes. provided repro with client logs and server stream id. client uses exponential backoff starting at 5s, doubling to 40s, then reconnect. they store resume_token but only send it in a `Prefer: resume_token=<token>; offset=<n>` header (custom). server currently expects Last-Event-ID header for resume.
Jordan: can you paste the logs and the curl repro? we should confirm header mismatch.
Alex: pasted from user (redacted):

```
# client reconnect snippet
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" -H "Prefer: resume_token=rt-12345; offset=128" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sse?model=redwood-2"

# client log around disconnect
[2026-01-18T10:11:02Z] SSE disconnected (code=1006)
[2026-01-18T10:11:02Z] scheduling reconnect in 5s
[2026-01-18T10:11:47Z] reconnect attempt with resume_token rt-12345 offset 128
```

Sam: server log for that session id (sid=svc-9876):
```
[2026-01-18T10:10:59Z] session open sid=svc-9876 resume_ttl=30s resume_token=rt-12345
[2026-01-18T10:11:30Z] session expired sid=svc-9876 reason=ttl
[2026-01-18T10:11:47Z] new session created sid=svc-3333 (resume_token mismatch) ip=1.2.3.4
[2026-01-18T10:11:48Z] generation started gid=g-5555 sid=svc-3333
[2026-01-18T10:11:50Z] client provided Prefer.resume_token=rt-12345 offset=128 but session not found
[2026-01-18T10:11:58Z] resumed partial stream: sent tokens 129-256
```

Maria: so server TTL was 30s. client waited ~45s and created a new session, which started a fresh generation (g-5555) and then separately the resume logic sent tokens 129-256. duplicate content occurs because the resumed tokens overlap with the fresh generation.
Jordan: and billing sees two generation start events and charges twice.
BillingBot: Alert: 2 generation charges logged for customer acct acct-444 (g-4444, g-5555). Please escalate if refund needed.

Alex: customer expects guidance: 1) how to avoid duplicates 2) whether they were charged incorrectly 3) if server can dedupe.
Sam: proposed customer guidance (short):
- keep reconnect backoff < session_resume_ttl (we default to 30s). prefer jittered linear backoff: 1s, 2s, 3s instead of doubling to 40s.
- send Last-Event-ID or X-Resume-Token header aligned with server expectations (we accept Last-Event-ID currently)
- include an idempotency header on generation-level actions: `X-Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` so server can dedupe new-generation creation across reconnects
- persist the resume token across app restarts and replay it immediately on reconnect

Maria: steps for us (internal):
- add a KB response for TTL vs backoff guidance (customer-facing)
- have billing team review acct-444 charges and hold refunds pending repro
- engineering: consider server-side safety: accept Prefer.resume_token format and attempt server-side offset reconciliation; if a new generation is created while a resume with overlapping offset arrives, prefer resume and cancel duplicate generation if possible.

Jordan: quick repro we used in staging to reproduce the double-charge/dup: start a gen, intentionally drop connection, wait for server ttl+5s, then reconnect with resume header; observe two generation-start events in logs and duplicate tokens emitted.

```
# repro script (high-level)
1) open sse connection -> start generation
2) kill connection (tcp) while generation mid-stream
3) sleep (resume_ttl + 5s)
4) reconnect with resume_token or Last-Event-ID
5) watch server logs for two gid start events
```

Sam: suggested immediate mitigation on platform: extend default resume_ttl to 90s for a week to reduce customer impact while we ship longer-term dedupe.
Alex: customers will like that short term. also add a warning in the API docs about recommended retry strategy and example client pseudocode.
Maria: example client pseudocode to recommend (for KB):

```
let backoff = 1; // seconds
while (!connected) {
  await connect();
  if (!connected) {
    await sleep(backoff + random(0, 0.2*backoff));
    backoff = Math.min(backoff + 1, 8); // linear up to 8s
  }
}

// on reconnect send headers:
// Last-Event-ID: <last-event-id>
// X-Idempotency-Key: <same-uuid-used-on-initial>
```

SupportBot: KB draft created: /kb/sse-reconnect-backoff-guidance (internal). Assigned to Maria.
Maria: I'll file a billing review with finance for acct-444 and attach logs.
BillingBot: Billing review ticket BR-2026 created for acct-444, flagged high-priority.

Alex: action items recap: Maria -> KB + billing ticket, Sam -> TTL bump trial, Jordan -> engineering ticket to support Prefer.resume_token and idempotency dedupe, Sam -> monitor for other occurrences and compile list of affected accounts.
Jordan: I'll open ENG-1234 with logs and a proposed server-side offset reconciliation algorithm. will include a short patch outline: when Prefer.resume_token present and session expired but resume token valid within last N minutes, attempt to reconcile offsets and cancel overlapping fresh generation.
Sam: thanks team. @Alex please send the customer the KB link and that we are reviewing billing asap.
Alex: sending now. :thumbsup:
Maria: tagging customer success lead for refunds: @Jordan -> can you confirm when ENG-1234 is created so we can update the customer timeline?
Jordan: will create ENG-1234 in ~30m and post link here.
Alex: thanks. closing loop once billing replies.
